title: AI invoice processing: buy an AP tool, then fix what it misses
description: 15 AP and invoice-capture tools checked, with prices where they exist. Why reading invoices is solved and exceptions and fraud are not.
summary: AI invoice processing reads a supplier invoice, codes it, matches it to the purchase order and gets it approved and paid. Reading the invoice now costs cents. The money is in the 18% of invoices that hit an exception, and in the fake ones that ask you to pay a new bank account.
verdict: Buy an accounts payable tool before you build anything: BILL, Ramp and Tipalti publish prices and already read invoices well. Then spend your effort where the suites fall short: the exceptions that stall approval, a check on any change to a supplier's bank details, and invoices from suppliers in countries that now require e-invoices. Build a custom AI step only for those gaps, and benchmark it on 50 of your own invoices first.

pickElse: Under a few hundred invoices a month and already on QuickBooks or Xero: use the bill capture built into your accounting software first.
Many entities, countries or currencies: look at the global suites (Tipalti, Coupa, Basware, Medius). Expect a contract and no list price.
You only need the data out of the invoice, not the workflow: a capture tool (Rossum, Nanonets, Docsumo) or a cloud invoice parser feeds your ERP directly.
You run Microsoft Power Platform: AI Builder has a prebuilt invoice model, limited to 360 calls a minute and 20 MB per file.

rules.name: Germany: B2B e-invoicing
rules.what: All businesses must be able to receive EN 16931 e-invoices since 1 Jan 2025. Larger firms must issue them from 2027 and nearly all from 2028.

rules.name: France: B2B e-invoicing
rules.what: Every business must be able to receive e-invoices; large and mid-size firms must issue them. Small firms issue from 1 Sep 2027.

rules.name: EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA)
rules.what: Member states can require e-invoicing; digital reporting for cross-border B2B starts 1 Jul 2030.

rules.name: United States
rules.what: No federal or state B2B e-invoicing mandate. A voluntary network exists. Source is a vendor that helped found it.

howToTest: Pull 50 recent invoices, including credit notes, multi-page invoices, foreign ones and the worst scans.
Write down the right supplier, number, date, total, tax and PO for each before any tool reads them.
Run each tool on the same set. Count wrong values apart from blanks: a wrong total is worse than a missing one.
Add three test invoices that change a supplier's bank details, and check each tool holds them.
Measure how many invoices go straight through with no person, and the cost per invoice including add-ons.

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy for the workflow: inbox, approvals, payments, ERP sync and an audit trail. Suites have solved this, and you do not want to own payments.
buyVsBuild.build: Build only the checks your suite misses: exception triage, fraud holds, odd document types, or coding rules specific to your business. These sit beside the suite, not instead of it.

watchOuts: The price you see is rarely the price you pay. Matching, payments, more entities and ERP sync are often add-ons.
Payment fraud rides on invoices. The AFP found 74% of US organizations were hit by business email compromise in 2025. Any change to bank details needs a call-back on a known number.
A tool that reads the subtotal as the total looks right at a glance. In our benchmark, 7 of 10 tools picked the wrong one of two look-alike tables.
E-invoices in Germany and France arrive as structured data. A tool that only reads PDFs will miss the point and the deadlines.
